quote: Journey to the West is full of gods and demons on the page, yet between the lines are written the words "ritual doctrine devours people." Wukong's golden headband is a shackle clamped onto thought itself.
The study of Journey to the West should begin from the genealogy of its editions; do not strain after political allegory — first get the facts straight.
The four pilgrims — Tang Sanzang and his disciples — are a revolutionary contingent: there is a united front, there is struggle, there is division, and there is final victory.
Read Journey to the West as you would sip tea — do not take it too seriously. Bajie's simple honesty and Wukong's monkey nature are life in its most genuine form.

The genius of Journey to the West lies in writing truth through absurdity: every demon is the ways of the world, every god and Buddha is merely human feeling, and a single brush links the three teachings.
Journey to the West is an epic, and Sun Wukong is the incarnation of rebellion; his golden staff shattered the old order of the celestial court.
